name: Knappenwelt Gurgltal Tarrenz
kurzbeschreibung: The Gurgltal Mining World in Tarrenz: authentically reconstructed 15th-century historical mining village with ore processing and a healer's garden.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Knappenwelt Gurgltal (Gurgltal Mining World) is idyllically situated at the foot of the Tschirgant mountain in the Strad district of Tarrenz near Imst in the Tyrolean Oberland, at an altitude of around 840 meters. Opened in 2008, this extensive open-air museum is an authentically reconstructed medieval mining village and is considered an outstanding historical mining monument in Tyrol. It provides a vivid impression of the heyday of Tyrolean ore mining in the 15th and 16th centuries, when the Gurgltal was one of Europe's most important lead mining sites, supplying the Fugger and Habsburg families with valuable raw materials.

Route & Requirements

The Knappenwelt consists of nine authentically reconstructed wooden and stone buildings, based on historical models, connected by narrow paths and watercourses. Visitors can explore the forge, the miner's house with authentically furnished sleeping quarters, the mine clerk's house, the ore processing plant with a functional wooden stamp mill, and the faithfully recreated mine tunnel. Engaging multimedia stations and audio guides (also available as a special children's tour) describe the extremely hard and dangerous daily life of the miners underground.

Visit & Arrival

The Knappenwelt Gurgltal is open from early May to late October, Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM (closed on Mondays; open daily in July and August). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €9.50, seniors approx. €8.50, children and teenagers (6 to 15 years) approx. €5.00, toddlers under 6 years free; family ticket approx. €22.00. Holders of the regional Urlaubspass Imst receive discounted admission. Arrival by car: Take the Inntalautobahn A12 to Imst, then continue on the B189 towards Nassereith/Fernpass to Tarrenz, Strad district; large free parking spaces are available directly at Knappenwelt 1. By public transport: ÖBB to Imst-Pitztal train station, from there take VVT bus line 4206 or 4208 every half hour to the Tarrenz Strad stop (approx. a five-minute walk to the entrance).

Tips

The entire area of the open-air museum is largely flat and easily accessible with strollers and all-terrain wheelchairs; handcarts for children can be rented at the ticket office. Children enjoy the gold and mineral washing stations, where they can sift real pyrites and semi-precious stones from the gravel. The historic inn Happis Hütte, located directly on the museum grounds, serves traditional Tyrolean miner's pans and refreshments, offering lasting, fascinating insights into the centuries-old, rich mining and cultural history of the Tyrolean Alps and its historical mining communities.
